title: Episode 122: ChatGPT, GTC 2023 & Stickers on our Foreheads

sentences.en: All of that stuff could be like a couple stickers on my forehead and a chip in my wriSt.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西就像是我额头上的几张贴纸和我手腕上的一个芯片。

sentences.en: Like, let's go.
sentences.zh: 比如说，我们走吧。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 快点。

sentences.en: I'm so tired.
sentences.zh: 我好累。

sentences.en: Like, we're going to, by the time we're 60, we're going to look back at the days when you would leave the house
sentences.zh: 比如说，等我们到60岁的时候，回想起那些日子，你会离开家

sentences.en: and you'd have to bring all this stuff, these headphones and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须带上所有这些东西，这些耳机和所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And it's just going to be, like, it's going to be in us or stickers on our foreheads.
sentences.zh: 然后它就会变成，比如说，它会植入我们体内或者作为我们额头上的贴纸。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP The Podcast, episode 122, recorded on March 21st, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 122 期，录制于 2023 年 3 月 21 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we chat about ChatGPT, the NVIDIA GTC conference, and intelligence augmentation.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天和我的联合主持人布莱斯一起，我们聊聊 ChatGPT、英伟达 GTC 大会以及智能增强。

sentences.en: We're back.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了。

sentences.en: We are back.
sentences.zh: 我们真的回来了。

sentences.en: Are we hopping straight into things?
sentences.zh: 我们要直接切入正题吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I got a thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我有个事。

sentences.en: If you got a thing, we can do your thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你有事，我们可以先聊你的事。

sentences.en: I don't really have any things, but I'll just start off by saying it has been...
sentences.zh: 我其实没什么事，但我先说一句，这已经……

sentences.en: What do you mean you don't have a thing?
sentences.zh: 你这话什么意思，怎么就没事？

sentences.en: I mean, I got tons of stuff, obviously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我有一堆事，显然。

sentences.en: Some nerve you have.
sentences.zh: 你还真好意思。

sentences.en: I just meant to say you said you had a topic to talk about, so I did not mentally prepare anything.
sentences.zh: 我只是想说你之前说有个话题要聊，所以我什么都没在脑子里准备。

sentences.en: That being said, we recorded with Zach back on February 16th.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们是在 2 月 16 日和扎克一起录的。

sentences.en: That was ages ago.
sentences.zh: 那都是好久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was five episodes, the most we've split up a single recording.
sentences.zh: 对，那是五期节目之前，是我们单次录制被拆分得最多的一次。

sentences.en: I got to tell you, I love Zach.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，我太喜欢扎克了。

sentences.en: Honestly, I was thinking that, I mean, usually we do our Christmas holiday special episode where we just chat, and it's usually just you and me.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我当时就在想，我是说，通常我们会在圣诞节假期做一期特别节目，大家就是随便聊聊，通常也就是你和我。

sentences.en: I feel like Zach would fit in great, even though it's like, you know, the annual tradition is it's just you and me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得扎克能完美融入进来，尽管你知道，年度传统是一直只有你和我。

sentences.en: But Zach was just fan.
sentences.zh: 但扎克真的太棒了。

sentences.en: I love how hard of a time he gives you.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢他怎么疯狂难为你了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: From a place of love.
sentences.zh: 出于爱意的刁难。

sentences.en: But he just had so many zingers, and I juSt...
sentences.zh: 但他有太多俏皮话了，而且我……

sentences.en: The cold opens of those...
sentences.zh: 那些节目的开场白……

sentences.en: You should just go listen to the first 30 seconds of each of the last five episodes because I think at least three or four of the five are him, like, ripping into you
sentences.zh: 你应该去听听过去五期节目每集的前 30 秒，因为我觉得最后五期里至少有三四期都是他在狂损你

sentences.en: about the authority-filling curve and, you know, Bryce is fancy.
sentences.zh: 关于那个权威填充曲线，还有，你知道的，布莱斯很讲究。

sentences.en: Anyways, it was...
sentences.zh: 总之，那……

sentences.en: It brings me a lot of joy to have someone like Zach, you know, try and bring you down to Earth, which, of course, he failed.
sentences.zh: 有像扎克这样的人，你知道，试图把你拉回现实，这给我带来很多快乐，当然他失败了。

sentences.en: He magnificently failed in doing that, but...
sentences.zh: 他在做这件事上惨败，但是……

sentences.en: I mean, it's pretty hard to bring you down to Earth.
sentences.zh: 我是说，要把你拉回现实挺难的。

sentences.en: It is amusing at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少还挺逗的。

sentences.en: I'm pretty much helium.
sentences.zh: 我简直就是氦气。

sentences.en: I just rise up.
sentences.zh: 我只会飘起来。

sentences.en: But yeah, we recorded that on February 16th, and then the last time we recorded before that was February 1St.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我们在 2 月 16 日录制了那期，然后在那之前我们录制的时间是 2 月 1 日。

sentences.en: So today is March 21st, which means that we actually, mano a mano, haven't chat in over a month and a half, which is probably pushing it in terms of...
sentences.zh: 所以今天是 3 月 21 日，这意味着我们两个面对面，已经有一个半月多没聊天了，就时间而言这大概有点久了……

sentences.en: I mean, I guess we've had multiple...
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想我们有过多次……

sentences.en: Well, I've been, like, off in the wilderness, you know, like, I've been...
sentences.zh: 好吧，我一直，像是，在荒野中，你知道的，就像我一直在……

sentences.en: Not the literal wilderness, although I do that sometimes too, but I've just been off and off exploring some things and messing around with some new projects.
sentences.zh: 不是字面意义上的荒野，虽然有时候我也那样，但我只是去探索了一些事情，折腾了一些新项目。

sentences.en: And so we haven't really...
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的没有……

sentences.en: We haven't even talked really at work.
sentences.zh: 我们在工作时甚至都没怎么聊过。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, we haven't really caught up.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，我们确实没怎么叙旧。

sentences.en: I mean, the most we did was...
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们做得最多的就是……

sentences.en: Although it's funny, the person who I've talked with the most at NVIDIA the past few weeks has actually been your boss.
sentences.zh: 虽然很有趣，过去几周在英伟达我聊得最多的人其实是你的老板。

sentences.en: Has it been Michael?
sentences.zh: 是迈克尔吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: I guess I did see that email thread about sort of the index.
sentences.zh: 我想我确实看到了关于索引的那封邮件串。

sentences.en: Well, that's like public stuff that's going to end up in a public API, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是那种最终会进入公开 API 的公开内容，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，那是……

sentences.en: Or is that your topic for today?
sentences.zh: 还是说那是你今天的主题？

sentences.en: I wrote a bunch of code and I just put it on GitHub and that's what we're going to talk about today, so...
sentences.zh: 我写了一堆代码，然后直接放到了 GitHub 上，这就是我们今天要聊的，所以……

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: Anyway, well, before we hop into that, is there any update?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，好吧，在我们切入正题之前，有什么更新吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we've been chatting, so I mean, I think the listener knows this by now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一直在聊天，所以我想听众现在也知道了。

sentences.en: If you're a regular listener, Bryce and I are definitely going to be in Europe together in June, we've got a road trip.
sentences.zh: 如果你是老听众，布莱斯和我六月份肯定会一起去欧洲，我们要去自驾游。

sentences.en: I guess you probably haven't booked that car, but we've got a road trip from like roughly the 18th...
sentences.zh: 我想你大概还没订那辆车吧，但我们有个自驾游，大约从 18 号开始……

sentences.en: I think I may have reserved the car.
sentences.zh: 我想我可能已经把车预订好了。

sentences.en: Have you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, we have the flights figured out.
sentences.zh: 不过对，我是说，机票我们已经搞定了。

sentences.en: I think the only thing now is we just got to figure out the hotels and then what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 现在唯一要确定的就是酒店，然后看看我们要干什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we'll be doing a little road trip.
sentences.zh: 对，所以我们要进行一次小小的自驾游。

sentences.en: And because of my other third podcast, which I actually did announce on this podcast back in January, it has launched my running podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为我的第三个播客，我 실제로 在今年 1 月的这个播客上宣布过，我的跑步播客已经上线了。

sentences.en: It's called Run for the Fun of It.
sentences.zh: 它叫“趣跑”（Run for the Fun of It）。

sentences.en: The name came from ChatGPT, of course, because whenever it comes to creative things, I think that's actually what ChatGPT is best at.
sentences.zh: 名字当然是 ChatGPT 想的，因为每当涉及到有创意的事情时，我觉得这正是 ChatGPT 最擅长的地方。

sentences.en: I used ChatGPT to write a heartfelt message to my girlfriend yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我昨天用 ChatGPT 给我的女朋友写了一条深情的信息。

sentences.en: But then I had so much fun doing it that afterwards I told her, because she was traveling yesterday and she was having a rough time because she forgot her credit cards at home.
sentences.zh: 但后来我玩得太开心了，以至于后来我告诉了她，因为她昨天在出差，而且过得很不顺利，因为她把信用卡忘在家了。

sentences.en: And so she was really stressed.
sentences.zh: 所以她压力真的很大。

sentences.en: And so I had DoorDash delivered to her from a restaurant that I knew she liked near where she's staying for work.
sentences.zh: 因此我通过 DoorDash 给她点了一份外卖，那是一家我知道她喜欢的餐馆，就在她出差住的地方附近。

sentences.en: And I had like a little message sent there, but it was like 120 character limit.
sentences.zh: 我还让人送去了一条简短的信息，但大概有 120 个字符的限制。

sentences.en: And I'm like, you know, I could just come up with something on my own or I could use artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我可以自己想点什么，或者我可以使用人工智能。

sentences.en: There's literally...
sentences.zh: 简直有……

sentences.en: I'll have to find the Instagram reel, but there's an Instagram reel of a comedian talking about writing a poem for this girl he liked and he used ChatGPT to do it.
sentences.zh: 我得找找那个 Instagram 短视频，但上面有一个喜剧演员在谈论为他喜欢的女孩写一首诗，他用了 ChatGPT 来写。

sentences.en: And then he admitted afterwards that he had used ChatGPT to do it and then she was offended.
sentences.zh: 然后他事后承认他用了 ChatGPT 来写，接着她就被冒犯了。

sentences.en: And so then she, whatever, they left parted ways after their date.
sentences.zh: 然后她，随便吧，他们约会结束后就各奔东西了。

sentences.en: And then the next day, he sent a heartfelt message apologizing.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他发了一条深情的信息道歉。

sentences.en: And then, you know, they ended up dating.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，他们最后还是在一起了。

sentences.en: And the punchline of the joke is that he got ChatGPT to write that heartfelt message.
sentences.zh: 这个笑话的包袱是，他让 ChatGPT 写了那条深情的信息。

sentences.en: Which, like, I mean, it's the thought that counts, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像是，我的意思是，礼轻情意重，对吧？

sentences.en: Ramona wasn't amused, but she's never really amused by me.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙娜觉得不好笑，但她从来没有觉得我好笑过。

sentences.en: It's the thought that counts.
sentences.zh: 心意最重要。

sentences.en: I think if you're taking the time to get a, I wouldn't call it sophisticated, but like sophisticated enough AI to assist you with the, you know, creative writing that you may not
sentences.zh: 我想如果你花时间去找一个，我不会称之为复杂的，但足够复杂的 AI 来协助你进行，你知道的，创意写作，你可能在这方面

sentences.en: be the best at, that's totally okay in my books.
sentences.zh: 不是最擅长，在我看来这完全没问题。

sentences.en: Well, but the funny thing is, I must have spent 40 minutes working with ChatGPT to write the message.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，我一定花了我 40 分钟和 ChatGPT 一起写那条信息。

sentences.en: That's part of the process.
sentences.zh: 那是过程的一部分。

sentences.en: Just because, like, I was having fun with it.
sentences.zh: 只是因为，像，我玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Prompt engineering.
sentences.zh: 提示词工程。

sentences.en: And so it probably took longer than it would have for me to write something on my own.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能比我自己写点东西花的时间还要长。

sentences.en: And, like, I'm actually a pretty good communicator.
sentences.zh: 而且，像，我其实是个挺擅长沟通的人。

sentences.en: So I think it probably would have been better, too.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得可能自己写会更好。

sentences.en: I don't know about that.
sentences.zh: 这我可说不准。

sentences.en: But I was just like, I'm a man on a mission.
sentences.zh: 但我当时就像是，我是一个有使命的人。

sentences.en: I feel like this is the hot thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这现在很火。

sentences.en: I'm going to do.
sentences.zh: 我要去做了。

sentences.en: I'm going to use it.
sentences.zh: 我要用它。

sentences.en: I feel like it's kind of like how when, was it Deep Blue beat Kasparov?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就有点像，当年是不是深蓝击败了卡斯帕罗夫？

sentences.en: And then they were like, oh, no, you know, computers are better at chess.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就觉得，哦，不，你知道的，电脑下国际象棋更厉害。

sentences.en: But then immediately after that, they had a contest where you could have computer-assisted humans.
sentences.zh: 但紧接着在那之后，他们举办了一个比赛，你可以让人工智能辅助人类。

sentences.en: Yeah, computer-assisted humans.
sentences.zh: 对，人工智能辅助人类。

sentences.en: And that was, like, the best combination.
sentences.zh: 那是，就像是，最好的组合。

sentences.en: Like, so a human with a computer was still better.
sentences.zh: 所以，配备了电脑的人类依然更厉害。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, actually, during our GTC Connect with the Experts session, typically when we do these Connect with the Experts sessions at GTC, and the C++ team at NVIDIA does one every year,
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，在我们 GTC 的“与专家连线”环节中，通常我们在 GTC 上做这些“与专家连线”环节时，英伟达的 C++ 团队每年都会做一次，

sentences.en: we tend to get a bunch of questions that are not strictly on topic.
sentences.zh: 我们往往会收到一堆并非严格切题的问题。

sentences.en: And one of the ones we got yesterday was about, I thought it was going to be off topic first because it was about ChatGPT, but it was actually very interesting.
sentences.zh: 昨天收到的其中一个问题，一开始我以为会偏题，因为它是关于 ChatGPT 的，但实际上非常有趣。

sentences.en: It was about, like, hey, can you use ChatGPT to auto-paralyze code?
sentences.zh: 它是关于，嘿，你能用 ChatGPT 来自动并行化代码吗？

sentences.en: And usually, if it's a question that I think is going to be off topic, I'm, like, a little reluctant to go and have us answer it live.
sentences.zh: 通常，如果这是一个我认为会偏题的问题，我就会，有点抗拒去现场回答它。

sentences.en: But then I actually read it, and I was like, ooh, this is actually, this opens up, like, an interesting topic of ChatGPT-assisted or large-language model-assisted programming,
sentences.zh: 但后来我仔细读了读，然后我想，哦，这其实，这开启了一个有趣的话题，关于 ChatGPT 辅助或大语言模型辅助编程，

sentences.en: which is something I've been thinking about a lot recently.
sentences.zh: 这也是我最近一直在思考的事情。

sentences.en: So, for a variety of reasons, one, I am lazy.
sentences.zh: 所以，出于各种原因，第一，我很懒。

sentences.en: I really just do not want to spend hours and hours cranking out code myself.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想花几个小时又几个小时自己去敲代码。

sentences.en: It just does not, it's not a good use of my time.
sentences.zh: 这根本不，这不是对我时间的有效利用。

sentences.en: But two, I have a bunch of ergonomic issues that limit the number of hours I can actually code.
sentences.zh: 但第二，我有一堆人体工学方面的问题，限制了我实际可以编码的小时数。

sentences.en: A bunch of, like, repetitive stress injury things from, you know, when I was, what?
sentences.zh: 一堆，像是，重复性劳损的问题，来自，你知道的，自我当时，什么？

sentences.en: You have RSI?
sentences.zh: 你有 RSI（重复性劳损）？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这事。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pretty common.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这挺常见的。

sentences.en: But, you know, that's one of the reasons why I don't do it.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这就是我为什么不这么做的原因之一。

sentences.en: You consider APL less characters.
sentences.zh: 你觉得 APL 用的字符更少。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: You know, the problem is, though, that you've got to type all those fancy characters, and you've got to use a bunch of key, like, key modifiers and layers to do that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，问题在于，你得输入所有那些花哨的字符，而且你必须使用一堆键，比如按键修改器和图层来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And that's actually supposed to make it worse.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上只会让情况更糟。

sentences.en: But anyways, long story short is, like, I would like to write more code, but I would not like to write more code, you know?
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，长话短说就是，我想写更多代码，但我又不想写更多代码，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I do know.
sentences.zh: 我懂。

sentences.en: So, I was thinking the other day, you know, until Elon perfects that little brain chip that we're all going to get implanted.
sentences.zh: 所以，我前几天在想，你知道的，在埃隆完善那个我们都要植入的小脑芯片之前。

sentences.en: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇，哇，哇，哇，哇。

sentences.en: Pause, pause, pause.
sentences.zh: 暂停，暂停，暂停。

sentences.en: You're actually going to put something that that crazy dude creates in your head?
sentences.zh: 你真的要把那个疯狂家伙创造的东西放进你的脑子里吗？

sentences.en: Well, not the one that he makes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是他造的那款。

sentences.en: But see, see what I figured, you know, he's really big on on dog fooding, right?
sentences.zh: 但你看，看看我是怎么想的，你知道的，他非常喜欢自己吃狗粮（践行自家产品），对吧？

sentences.en: I was reading this article the other day about that, that Elon, you know, a Tesla, a lot of the testing got done by, like, the executives, including Elon.
sentences.zh: 我前几天看到一篇文章说，埃隆，在特斯拉，很多测试都是由高管完成的，包括埃隆。

sentences.en: Like, a lot of the testing for autopilot would be like, Elon would go and, like, drive his Tesla with autopilot.
sentences.zh: 比如，自动驾驶的很多测试就像是，埃隆会去开着他的特斯拉使用自动驾驶。

sentences.en: And then, like, he would send a bunch of bug reports.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像是，他会发送一堆错误报告。

sentences.en: And then, like, that was their process.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像是，这就是他们的流程。

sentences.en: Like, Elon would go and drive the car and then, like, tell the engineers, like, go fix these things.
sentences.zh: 就像埃隆去开车，然后，像是，告诉工程师们，去修复这些东西。

sentences.en: Instead of, you know, having a more principled process.
sentences.zh: 而不是，你知道的，采用一个更有原则的流程。

sentences.en: But, you know, I got to figure that Elon's going to be one of the first people to install this chip.

sentences.en: And I think that's just my, the curmudgeon-y old man inside of me that is just inherently skeptical at any new thing.

sentences.en: Yeah, there was on that, on that live stream that you crashed a couple weeks ago, there was a number of comments being, like,

sentences.zh: 这家伙怎么没开语法高亮？

sentences.en: And it's, like, you know, half the time it's, like, I don't even want, like, some fancy builds.

sentences.en: But I think things like chat GPT are so promising and have such potential to transform how we operate that I'm actually interested in

sentences.zh: 改进我的开发工具箱。

sentences.en: And, and so, so I was, I was, I've been thinking a bit about, like, how, what would I actually want?
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，我一直在思考，到底，我真正想要的是什么？

sentences.en: You know, I think it's pretty clear that the, the correct interface for, like, pair programming with, with an AI is not logging into chat GPT and, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得很明显，和AI进行结对编程的正确交互方式，不是登录ChatGPT，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: asking it to do things and then copying and pasting output from it into another window and then trying it and then, you know, giving it feedback.
sentences.zh: 让它做这做那，然后把输出复制粘贴到另一个窗口，接着试跑，然后，你知道的，给它反馈。

sentences.en: Like, like, like, that's a lot of copying and pasting.
sentences.zh: 真的，这有太多的复制粘贴了。

sentences.en: I don't want to, I don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不想，我不想这么干。

sentences.en: I think I want, I think I'd want something more like, you know, the GitHub Copilot where it's integrated into your IDE and, like, as you start, you know, typing out stuff, it,
sentences.zh: 我想，我更想要那种类似于GitHub Copilot的东西，它集成在你的IDE里，然后，当你开始，你知道的，敲代码时，它

sentences.en: Um, but, but then it, that, so, so, so, so something that's like built into your IDE, um, uh, and that, you know, can get feedback from, uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，但是，但是，所以，所以，所以，所以就是那种内置在你的IDE里，呃，而且，你知道的，能从

sentences.en: your IDE was like the first thing I was thinking about.
sentences.zh: 你的IDE获取反馈的东西，这是我首先想到的。

sentences.en: And then I was thinking a bit about the problem of, well, what if you've got like a really big code base?
sentences.zh: 然后我又琢磨了一下这个问题：如果你的代码库非常庞大，那该怎么办？

sentences.en: Um, you know, like, like, what if I, what if what I want to tell the AI to do is like, hey, AI, I have this 1 million line, like, internal proprietary code base.

sentences.en: It's not part of your training set.
sentences.zh: 它不在你的训练集里面。

sentences.en: Um, like, and I want you to write me a PR for that, that does this thing in this code base.
sentences.zh: 呃，然后我希望你为这个代码库写一个PR，来实现某个功能。

sentences.en: Um, and the problem there is that even GPT-4 has a fairly limited input size.

sentences.en: Like, you could maybe feed in, like, you know, let's say 100 pages of text or something, but you probably couldn't feed in a million line code base, right, um, to it.
sentences.zh: 比如，你大概只能喂给它，你知道的，比方说100页的文本或者类似的东西，但你大概没法把一百万行的代码库喂给它，对吧，呃，没办法。

sentences.en: Um, and so asking it to do, to make some change across a large code base, uh, not clear to me how exactly we'd go about doing that yet.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以要求它在一个大型代码库中做出某些修改，呃，我还不太清楚我们具体该怎么做。

sentences.en: Um, but, but once I started thinking about that, it started occurring to me that, you know,
sentences.zh: 呃，不过，当我开始思考这个问题时，我突然意识到，你知道的，

sentences.en: what I really just want is I want to be able to go onto GitHub and file an issue against my project that describes the change that I want.

sentences.en: And then the AI opens up a PR that, um, uh, you know, implements that issue.

sentences.en: And then I can give it feedback in the PR saying like, okay, well, no, no, this is broken here.
sentences.zh: 接着我可以在PR里给它反馈，说，好吧，不对，不对，这里坏了。

sentences.en: And also importantly that because it's opening up a PR, it will get feedback from your CI results and whatnot.

sentences.en: So then it can go in, you know, you don't even have to tell it, hey, you know, this, this code that you wrote for me,
sentences.zh: 所以它就能进去，你知道的，你甚至都不用告诉它，嘿，你知道的，你为我写的这段代码，

sentences.en: it doesn't actually compile because it'll figure it out on its own when it sends the PR in.
sentences.zh: 其实没法编译，因为它在提交PR时自己就能搞清楚。

sentences.en: So that's more or less the interface that I settled up on wanting is then it doesn't matter what I, you know, you don't need to use a particular ID or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我最终确定的交互界面，这样一来，不管我，你知道的，你不需要使用特定的IDE什么的。

sentences.en: It's just, you just, I just type up a high level description of what I want and an issue.
sentences.zh: 很简单，你只需要在Issue里写一段对你想要的功能的高层次描述。

sentences.en: And then the AI goes out and does it.
sentences.zh: 然后AI就会去把它实现。

sentences.en: So, uh, somebody at Microsoft or GitHub or open AI, you know, get on that, get on that.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，微软、GitHub或OpenAI的某位大牛，你知道的，快把这个搞定吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like it's incredibly doable for a certain category of issue.

sentences.en: And if I could just ask some, like, I think that I've talked about this on this podcast before is that it's called GPT duck or duck GPT,

sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这好像是在贬低整整一，你知道的，某一类人群的工作，但我们确实不是构建工程师，或者说至少对我自己而言，
